imc-brief-xfinity-home-wifi.md.line: The living room has three agendas and one internet connection holding the meeting.
imc-brief-xfinity-home-wifi.md.tension: A shared household treats work, homework, and entertainment like separate worlds, even though they all converge through the same home internet.

imc-brief-xfinity-home-wifi.md.line: One home can contain a meeting, a math problem, and a movie night.
imc-brief-xfinity-home-wifi.md.tension: Shared households often ask one internet connection to support very different activities happening at the same time.

imc-brief-xfinity-home-wifi.md.line: The kitchen table can be an office, a classroom, and a theater before dinner.
imc-brief-xfinity-home-wifi.md.tension: A shared household needs one home internet role to make sense across very different daily activities in the same space.

imc-brief-xfinity-home-wifi.md.line: The category talks like a utility; shared homes behave like a traffic pattern.
imc-brief-xfinity-home-wifi.md.tension: Category convention challenged: home internet is usually framed as a utility or technical service, while this brief asks us to frame the household's moving pattern of work, homework and entertainment.

imc-brief-xfinity-home-wifi.md.line: Every screen in the house has a different job at the same time.
imc-brief-xfinity-home-wifi.md.tension: Shared households feel ordinary online life as a pileup of work, homework and entertainment, while the brand must stay human-first rather than technical.

imc-brief-xfinity-mobile-v2.md.line: The phone runs the day; the plan should not get a speaking role.
imc-brief-xfinity-mobile-v2.md.tension: People depend on their phones for nearly everything, yet the service decision itself feels like one more needy app in their life.

imc-brief-xfinity-mobile-v2.md.line: The family group chat should be messy; choosing mobile service should not.
imc-brief-xfinity-mobile-v2.md.tension: Phones carry the chaos of shared family life, but people do not want the same chaos when deciding on mobile service.

imc-brief-xfinity-mobile-v2.md.line: The phone can run the day without the plan hijacking it.
imc-brief-xfinity-mobile-v2.md.tension: The audience depends on their phone constantly, but resents when choosing mobile service becomes another task competing for attention.

imc-brief-xfinity-mobile-v2.md.line: The phone plan should stop acting like another device to manage.
imc-brief-xfinity-mobile-v2.md.tension: Category convention challenged: mobile brands often make the plan itself feel like an active thing people must compare, manage, and think about.

imc-brief-xfinity-mobile-v2.md.line: When the phone runs everything, choosing mobile shouldn't become another chore.
imc-brief-xfinity-mobile-v2.md.tension: The brand wants recognizable everyday phone behavior, but the campaign must avoid making mobile choice feel like another complicated task in that same day.
